prompt: Order the steps a developer follows to get a feature into the main codebase.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: A teammate reviews and approves it
Commit the changes on the branch
Create a feature branch from main
Merge the pull request into main

task.explanation: Branch, commit, open a PR, get it reviewed, then merge.

segments.text: Every ticket gets its own branch named after the ticket, e.g. feature/APP-142-login.
Developers push straight to main when they're in a hurry.
segments.issue: Skips review and can break the shared codebase; main should only change through reviewed PRs.

segments.text: Every pull request needs one approving review before merge.
Pull requests should be as large as possible to save review time.
segments.issue: Large PRs are slow to review and hide bugs; keep them small.

prompt: Your team tracks pull-request review time. Work out the average time from PR opened to approved, and how many PRs missed the 24-hour target.

task.prompt: Calculate each value from the data.
task.explanation: Average = (6 + 30 + 12 + 48 + 4) / 5 = 100 / 5 = 20 hours. PR-2 (30 h) and PR-4 (48 h) missed the target.

prompt: A developer says their feature is finished, but the Jira ticket shows the pull request has been waiting for review for three days. Sprint review is tomorrow.

task.prompt: A developer says their feature is finished, but the Jira ticket shows the pull request has been waiting for review for three days. Sprint review is tomorrow.

steps.question: What do you do?
options: Mark the story as done
Raise it at stand-up and ask who can review it today
Merge it yourself
Move it to next sprint without asking
steps.explanation: Unreviewed work is not done; unblock the review by making the wait visible.

steps.question: This keeps happening. What process change helps?
options: Remove code review
Agree a review turnaround (e.g. same day) and limit work in progress so people review before starting new work
Have the PM review all code
Only review at the end of the sprint
steps.explanation: An explicit review agreement and WIP limits keep PRs moving.

prompt: A critical bug is found in production while the main branch already contains half-finished features for the next release.

task.prompt: A critical bug is found in production while the main branch already contains half-finished features for the next release.

steps.question: How should the fix be made?
options: Fix it on main and release everything
Create a hotfix branch from the production release, fix, test and release just that
Wait for the next release
Edit the code directly on the server
steps.explanation: A hotfix branch from what is in production ships the fix without unfinished features.

steps.question: After the hotfix is released, what must happen?
options: Nothing
Merge the fix back into main so it is not lost in the next release
Delete the main branch
Revert the hotfix
steps.explanation: Otherwise the next release from main would bring the bug back.

prompt: Why do PMs ask developers to include the ticket ID in branch names and PR titles?

options: It links code changes to tickets, so progress and release contents can be traced
Git requires it
It makes the code run faster
It replaces testing
mcq.explanation: Traceability lets Jira show linked PRs and helps build release notes.
